title: Eating Your Way Through İzmir: A Two-Day Plan From Boyoz to Urla
excerpt: İzmir's food runs from boyoz and kumru in the bazaar to olive-oil greens and Michelin-listed tables in Urla. Here is how to structure one or two days so you taste the city, not just its famous names.

body.text: İzmir is better known as a gateway to Ephesus than as a food destination, yet it has one of Türkiye's most distinctive kitchens: Sephardic pastries at breakfast, a sandwich named after a bird, wild greens dressed in olive oil, and a wine and restaurant scene in nearby Urla that includes İzmir's first two-Michelin-star restaurant. In a column on 2 November 2026, the food writer Aylin Öney Tan summed up the city's appeal in [Hürriyet Daily News](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/opinion/aylin-oney-tan/from-street-food-to-starred-chefs-izmirs-flavor-stops-228871): "The stars may shine in Urla, but their light comes from the streets of İzmir." This guide turns that idea into a practical plan.
The dishes to know before you arrive

items: Boyoz: a flaky, oil-rich pastry of Sephardic origin, usually eaten in the morning; Michelin's travel feature describes it served with a boiled egg.
Gevrek: İzmir's name for the sesame bread ring known elsewhere in Türkiye as simit.
Kumru: a sesame-crusted sandwich named after the turtle dove. Michelin's feature calls the version with tulum cheese and tomato the true İzmir classic.
Söğüş: cold boiled meat from the head, cheek and tongue, served in bread with tomato, onion and parsley — a Kemeraltı stop on GoTürkiye's route, though not for every visitor.

Olive-oil dishes and wild greens: the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism's İzmir directorate](https://izmir.ktb.gov.tr/EN-348311/gastronomy-tourism.html) calls olive oil the primary basis of İzmir's culinary culture and describes herbs boiled briefly and served with lemon and olive oil. [GoTürkiye's İzmir taste page](https://goturkiye.com/izmir/taste) also lists samphire, artichoke hearts and zucchini flowers.
Sweets: İzmir lokma (small fried dough balls in syrup) and şambali (a semolina cake) both carry geographical indications, according to the ministry directorate.

body.text: Day one: the city's street food

[GoTürkiye's two-day İzmir street food route](https://goturkiye.com/routes/izmir-street-food-2-day-itinerary) is a good spine for a first day, and it names no restaurants, which leaves you free to follow the queues. Start with boyoz in Konak, then walk the Kordon waterfront and Sevgi Yolu in Alsancak. Head into Kemeraltı, the historic bazaar, for söğüş and şambali; the ministry directorate notes that Kemeraltı, Alsancak and Basmane are home to long-established restaurants and markets. Finish back on the Kordon in the evening with kumru and midye dolma, the stuffed mussels sold along the water.
Pace matters more than the list. Share portions, eat one thing at each stop and walk between them; a bazaar day goes wrong when lunch at noon leaves no room for anything after two o'clock.
Day two: choose between the other shore and Urla

GoTürkiye's second day crosses the bay: gevrek in Karşıyaka, kokoreç in Bornova and fried mussels, ending at sunset in Bostanlı. It is the better choice if you want to see everyday İzmir. The alternative is Urla, which Öney Tan places about an hour's drive from the city. Michelin's travel feature describes Urla's wine road as İzmir's most famous wine route, with vineyards a 30–45 minute drive by rental car or taxi, and calls Havra Street, in the Kemeraltı bazaar, a culinary hotspot in the city itself.
If you go to Urla for a special meal, book ahead and do not drive if you plan to taste wine. A taxi or a driver for the day turns a stressful logistics problem into a relaxed afternoon.
What the Michelin Guide actually says about İzmir

The [Michelin Guide's 2026 Türkiye selection](https://guide.michelin.com/en/article/michelin-guide-ceremony/the-michelin-guide-turkiye-reveals-its-2026-restaurant-selection), announced in December 2025, made Vino Locale in Urla İzmir's first two-star restaurant and gave Teruar Urla, already starred, a Green Star for sustainability. As of November 2026, Michelin's [İzmir listing](https://guide.michelin.com/us/en/izmir/restaurants) shows 29 restaurants across the province, including four starred restaurants and nine Bib Gourmands, which recognise good cooking at moderate prices. Michelin is due to announce its 2027 Türkiye selection in early December 2026, so these awards may change. The Hürriyet Daily News column cited above lists Vino Locale with one star and a Green Star; Michelin's own pages show Vino Locale with two stars and the Green Star at Teruar Urla, so check Michelin directly before you book around a star.

For most visitors, the Bib Gourmand list is the more useful tool: it points to places where a regular lunch shows off local cooking without a tasting-menu commitment. Use the stars for one planned evening, not for the whole trip.

items: Base yourself near Alsancak or Konak so day one is walkable.
Plan boyoz for breakfast; most bakeries are busiest early.
Leave a gap between a heavy bazaar lunch and an evening on the Kordon.
Book Urla restaurants in advance and arrange transport before you set out.
Look for the Alaçatı Herb Festival and Urla International Artichoke Festival, both listed by the ministry directorate, and confirm dates locally because they change each year.

body.text: If you are building a wider food trip, compare this plan with our [Gaziantep food weekend](/blog/gaziantep-food-weekend-planning), which follows the same time-of-day approach in the southeast. For the city itself, see our [İzmir destination page](/destinations/izmir), and our [Turkish Riviera guide](/blog/turkish-riviera-antalya-bodrum-fethiye-guide) if you are continuing south along the coast.

seo.intent: Plan one or two food-focused days in İzmir: which local dishes to try, where to eat them, and whether to add Urla.
seo.uniqueValue: A two-day İzmir eating plan built on GoTürkiye's route, the ministry directorate's culinary notes and Michelin's own 2026 listing, noting where press coverage differs from Michelin's own 2026 listing and explaining when Urla is worth the trip.

quality.reviewNotes: Prepared 2026-11-10 from a research fact sheet. Independent EN fact check opened all seven sources (HDN column 2 Nov 2026, GoTürkiye route and taste pages, İzmir ktb directorate gastronomy page, Michelin 2026 selection announcement, Michelin İzmir listing, Michelin travel feature) and required fixes were applied: Michelin framing corrected (Vino Locale two stars; Teruar Urla starred plus Green Star; 29 listed, 4 starred, 9 Bib Gourmand 'as of November 2026'); the 2027 selection caveat added (announcement due early Dec 2026); HDN-vs-Michelin award discrepancy stated transparently; Öney Tan line quoted exactly; Havra Street attribution and festival wording fixed; unsourced embellishments removed. No restaurant ranking, prices or first-hand tastings. Independent DE/zh-CN/KO/ES translation review with fixes applied (restored taxi, removed an added star count). Not a human or native-speaker certification.
